problem: Disney wanted a direct relationship with viewers of its own films and shows.
title: Disney launches Disney+ at $6.99 a month and reports 10 million sign-ups in a day
context: Disney entered the streaming market against Netflix and others.
decision_made: Launch Disney+ at $6.99 a month, with a $12.99 bundle with Hulu and ESPN+.
action_taken: Launched on 12 November 2019 in the US, Canada and the Netherlands, with a seven-day free trial and a year free offered to some Verizon customers.
observed_outcome: Disney reported over 10 million sign-ups within a day and shares reached a record high. Launch-day glitches occurred, and it was unclear how many sign-ups were paying.
lessons: A strong content library and low price can produce a fast start, but sign-ups are not the same as paying subscribers.
limitations: Very short window. Sign-ups include free trials and promotions, and Disney did not say whether presales were included.

claims.claim_text: Disney launched Disney+ at $6.99 a month on 12 November 2019.
Disney said Disney+ had more than 10 million sign-ups one day after launch.
